known_facts_book1: The King and ruler of all the nomes at the time of this story, seated on an ivory throne, a little round man with a pointed beard and hair rising to a tall curl on top of his head.
Wears a diamond crown and silken robes with buttons of cut rubies, and carries a golden sceptre with a big jeweled ball at one end.

Recognizes King Gos's story as a clever lie 'woven without a thread of truth' and takes the treasure and the prisoners anyway, on the stated policy that powerful Kings must stand together and trample the weaker underfoot.
Refuses to touch anyone under Ozma's protection, saying Ozma of Oz is far more powerful than he is.
Treats his captives more considerately than King Gos did, having Klik remove their chains once their door is locked.
Has his second-best crown mashed when Bilbil throws him against a jeweled wall, and is not in the least amused.
Owns the Three Trick Caverns, from which no one has escaped alive in hundreds of years, and pivots Inga's whole bedroom on its axis to feed him into them.
Tries on Rinkitink in turn: falling rocks, a skein of golden thread that weaves itself into a net, a trapdoor over the Bottomless Gulf, and a cavern of flying knives — every one of which fails.
Makes a joke of the knives — telling them to be 'pieceful' — and is not laughed at.
Loses his own crown to Rinkitink in a wager that Inga has died in the caverns, and greets the boy's survival with 'Tarts and tadpoles!'
Gives up the captives the instant Dorothy begins to lift the cover from her basket of eggs, pleading with his teeth chattering.
Suffers a severe headache from revelling with Gos and Cor, which makes him unusually cross when Inga first arrives.

known_relations_book1.King Gos: The King who bribes him to keep the prisoners, and whose lie he sees through.
known_relations_book1.Inga: The boy he tries and fails to destroy in the Three Trick Caverns.
known_relations_book1.Rinkitink: The King whose magic he cannot overcome and to whom he loses his crown in a wager.
known_relations_book1.Klik: His chamberlain, who carries his orders.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The Princess of Oz whose eggs make him surrender at once.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler he dares not offend.

known_facts_book1: The nome who wears a gold collar around his neck and carries a bunch of golden keys, and serves as King Kaliko's chamberlain.
Escorts King Gos and Queen Cor and their prisoners into the royal presence, and later leads Kitticut and Garee to a small cavern, removes their chains and gives them a good supper.
Tells the visitors they are neither prisoners nor welcome guests, and bids them 'Eat hearty, sleep tight, and pleasant dreams to you.'
Presses the secret spring that opens the wall and reveals Inga alive after the Three Trick Caverns.
Runs in with his hair standing on end to report that the Wizard of Oz and Dorothy are approaching, and tells Inga that Dorothy is a terrible foe to deal with.
Is the name Inga must call aloud, after clapping four times, to be admitted to the Nome King's caverns.

known_relations_book1.Kaliko: His King, whose orders he carries out.
known_relations_book1.Inga: Whom he guides in and out of the caverns.
known_relations_book1.King Kitticut: Whose chains he removes and whom he feeds.

known_facts_book1: Two of the crooked nomes who spring from the ground around King Gos and Queen Cor at the unguarded entrance to the caverns.
The Long-Eared Hearer has very long ears and says he heard the visitors coming early that morning.
The Lookout has eyes that look in different directions at the same time, curiously bright and penetrating, and can see over a hill or around a corner; he says he saw them coming the day before.
Appear in one scene only, to prove that the Nome King already expects his visitors, and take no further part in the story.

known_relations_book1.Kaliko: Their King, who is forewarned by them.
known_relations_book1.King Gos: The visitor whose approach they detect.
